content:
You plan to visit 9 European cities for 30 days in total. You only take direct flights to commute between cities. You want to spend 5 days in Santorini. You would like to meet your friends at Santorini between day 25 and day 29 to tour together. You want to spend 5 days in Krakow. You are going to attend a wedding in Krakow between day 18 and day 22. You want to spend 5 days in Paris. You want to meet a friend in Paris between day 11 and day 15. You plan to stay in Vilnius for 3 days. You plan to stay in Munich for 5 days. You would like to visit Geneva for 2 days. You plan to stay in Amsterdam for 4 days. You want to spend 5 days in Budapest. You want to spend 4 days in Split.

Here are the cities that have direct flights:
Paris and Krakow, Paris and Amsterdam, Paris and Split, from Vilnius to Munich, Paris and Geneva, Amsterdam and Geneva, Munich and Split, Split and Krakow, Munich and Amsterdam, Budapest and Amsterdam, Split and Geneva, Vilnius and Split, Munich and Geneva, Munich and Krakow, from Krakow to Vilnius, Vilnius and Amsterdam, Budapest and Paris, Krakow and Amsterdam, Vilnius and Paris, Budapest and Geneva, Split and Amsterdam, Santorini and Geneva, Amsterdam and Santorini, Munich and Budapest, Munich and Paris.

Find a trip plan of visiting the cities for 30 days by taking direct flights to commute between them.

Please output the trip plan in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"day_range": "Day X-Y", "place": "<CITY>"}]}. Include all city visits with their day ranges. Do not include separate flight entries in the JSON output.

IMPORTANT: When you fly from city A to city B on day X, that day counts for BOTH cities. For example:
- If you stay in Venice from Day 1-3 and fly to Vienna on Day 3, then:
  - Venice: Day 1-3 (3 days)
  - Vienna: Day 3-6 (4 days, including the flight day)
- The flight day (Day 3) is counted for both Venice and Vienna.
- Do NOT create separate flight entries in the JSON.

Below is one valid solution. In this plan the nine cities are visited in the order below. Note that the “flight‐day overlap” rule is used so that, for example, Budapest is “visited” on Days 1–5 while Amsterdam is visited on Days 5–8 (since Day 5 counts for both places). Also, the three “event” cities occur at times that let you meet your friend in Paris during Days 11–15, attend the Krakow wedding with at least one day between Days 18 and 22, and then meet your Santorini‐friend during the Santorini stay (which covers Days 26–30, so that a meeting between Days 26–29 is possible).

One correct itinerary is as follows:

• Segment 1 – Budapest (5 days). With no prior flight, you start in Budapest on Day 1 and stay through Day 5.

• Segment 2 – Amsterdam (4 days). You fly from Budapest to Amsterdam on Day 5 (so Day 5 counts for both cities) and remain in Amsterdam until Day 8.

• Segment 3 – Split (4 days). A direct flight exists from Amsterdam to Split (remember that flying occurs on the first day in Split). Thus you are in Split from Day 8 through Day 11.

• Segment 4 – Paris (5 days). With a flight from Split to Paris on Day 11 (allowed via the “Paris and Split” connection), you are in Paris from Day 11 to Day 15. (Your friend‐meeting in Paris may take place on, say, Day 11 or later but no later than Day 15.)

• Segment 5 – Krakow (5 days). There is a direct flight from Paris to Krakow. Thus Krakow is visited from Day 15 to Day 19. (The wedding in Krakow can happen late in this segment – e.g. on Day 18 or 19 – which lies in the required [18–22] window.)

• Segment 6 – Vilnius (3 days). Note that the only direct flight from Krakow to Vilnius is the one “from Krakow to Vilnius.” Hence you fly on Day 19 and then remain in Vilnius through Day 21.

• Segment 7 – Munich (5 days). The only available flight from Vilnius is “from Vilnius to Munich.” So you leave Vilnius on Day 21 and then are in Munich from Day 21 to Day 25.

• Segment 8 – Geneva (2 days). From Munich you take a direct flight to Geneva (Munich and Geneva are connected), arriving on Day 25. You remain there through Day 26.

• Segment 9 – Santorini (5 days). Finally, a direct flight exists from Geneva to Santorini. Flying on Day 26 puts you in Santorini from Day 26 to Day 30. (Your Santorini friend–meeting can be arranged on one of Days 26–29.)

Notice that all flight legs obey the connectivity rules (for example, the crucial directed flights—Krakow → Vilnius and Vilnius → Munich—occur in the proper order) and the event times fall in the proper parts of the itinerary.

Below is the JSON output of this valid trip plan:

{
  "itinerary": [
    {"day_range": "Day 1-5", "place": "Budapest"},
    {"day_range": "Day 5-8", "place": "Amsterdam"},
    {"day_range": "Day 8-11", "place": "Split"},
    {"day_range": "Day 11-15", "place": "Paris"},
    {"day_range": "Day 15-19", "place": "Krakow"},
    {"day_range": "Day 19-21", "place": "Vilnius"},
    {"day_range": "Day 21-25", "place": "Munich"},
    {"day_range": "Day 25-26", "place": "Geneva"},
    {"day_range": "Day 26-30", "place": "Santorini"}
  ]
}

This 38‑“city‐day” sum (5+4+4+5+5+3+5+2+5) minus 8 overlapping flight days equals exactly 30 days.
